title: Clinical Research Administrator
company: SPD Development Company Ltd - Agency - Contract
description:
Clinical Research Administrator

Salary: £30,000 to £35,000 depending on skills and experience + Benefits + Bonus

Location: Bedford

The Vacancy

12-month Fixed Term Contract starting January 2027

We are looking for a Clinical Research Administrator to provide support, conduct and monitoring of Clinical studies within the wider Clinical programme ensuring compliance with study protocols and GCP. This will include study preparation, preparation of supplies, volunteer recruitment, study conduct and tracking activities.

SPD (Swiss Precision Diagnostics) are world leaders in the research, design and supply of advanced consumer diagnostic products. SPD is a joint venture business between P&G and Abbott, and our brand Clearblue is recognised the world over as providing accurate home pregnancy and fertility monitoring tests.

In this role you will be contributing and supporting internal Clinical studies which involves:
- Set-up activities, including sourcing study supplies, packaging and shipment of supplies.
- Tracking study status, inputting into study conduct meetings and reporting of study status.
- Contributing to study administration and execution activities volunteer recruitment, printing, collation, packing, payment, source data verification and testing.
- Administering and recording volunteer payments for studies.
- Supporting study team meetings and maintaining inspection-ready documentation.

We are looking for individuals who have:
- Good communication skills, both written and verbal, with excellent telephone skills. Previous experience of telephone work is desirable.
- Excellent attention to detail and must be highly organised.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint and Excel).
- Ideally a Bachelor s Degree in Biomedical Science or a related field.
- Ideally experience with clinical studies.
- Ideally knowledge of IVDR, ISO20916 and ISO13485.
- The personal attributes, attitude and mindset of Results focused, Self-aware and a Team player.

We want you to join us and actively work with colleagues across the business to achieve great things for people in their reproductive life.

We can offer you:
- An excellent working environment
- 25 days paid annual leave plus bank holidays
- Company pension scheme including competitive employer s contribution
- Private Medical Insurance package with additional medical cash plan scheme
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Company supported employee Health and Wellbeing programme
- Life assurance
- Free plentiful car parking and electrical car charging points
- Beautiful parkland setting with excellent transportation links to Cambridge, Milton Keynes and London

Right to Work

All candidates will be asked to provide proof of eligibility to work in the UK at interview.

Due to the requirements laid out by UK Visas and Immigration regarding Right to Work in the UK, SPD can only accept applications from individuals who currently have a status allowing them to work in the UK for this position.

We regret that we are unable to offer sponsorship for this role.

Equality

SPD is committed to providing a vibrant, ethical, and sustainable work environment that values equality, diversity, and inclusion.

If you require any reasonable adjustments to support you, at any stage during the application process, just let us know how we can help.

The Company

Swiss Precision Diagnostics GmbH (SPD) is a world leader in the research, design and marketing of advanced consumer diagnostic products.

Our SPD research centre is at the cutting edge of innovation and is fully engaged in the development of reliable diagnostic products to empower women on their reproductive journey. We are committed to answering the needs of our existing and future consumers, through a continuous flow of new and innovative products.

Interested

Click apply and you will be redirected to our careers page to complete your application.

title: Youth Employability Activity Coordinator - Bedfordshire
description:
Job Role: Youth Employability Activity Coordinator
Youth Engagement Employability Community Programmes Careers & Progression
Location: Bedfordshire - Community-Based (Local Travel Required)
Salary: £32,000 per annum
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time

Role Overview
Are you passionate about engaging young people, building confidence and creating opportunities that lead to meaningful careers?
We are recruiting an energetic and creative Youth Employability Activity Coordinator to design and deliver engaging programmes that help young people aged 18-24 develop the skills, confidence and motivation needed to progress into employment, education or training.
This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with experience in youth work, employability, education, careers guidance, community development, coaching, sports development, creative arts, training or support services who enjoys inspiring young people and helping them achieve their potential.
As a Youth Employability Activity Coordinator, you will create and deliver innovative workshops, projects and activities that develop employability skills, workplace awareness, resilience and confidence. Working closely with Mentors, employers and community partners, you will help participants take positive steps towards sustainable employment and long-term success.

Key Responsibilities
Activity Design & Delivery
- Design and deliver engaging, employment-focused activities for young people aged 18-24.
- Develop a rolling programme of workshops, projects and group activities aligned to participant goals and progression plans.
- Deliver sessions focused on:
- Employability skills
- Confidence building
- Teamwork
- Communication
- Digital skills
- Workplace readiness
- Personal development
- Utilise creative themes including:
- Sport
- Gaming
- Technology
- Virtual Reality
- Creative Arts
- Community Projects
- Volunteering Opportunities
- Adapt delivery to suit different learning styles, confidence levels and support needs.

Participant Engagement & Development
- Build positive, trusting relationships with young people.
- Use strengths-based and trauma-informed approaches to engagement.
- Support participants to identify their strengths, interests and aspirations.
- Help individuals develop:
- Communication skills
- Problem-solving abilities
- Resilience
- Professional behaviours
- Time management
- Confidence and self-belief
- Support learners to identify and articulate transferable skills for employment applications and interviews.

Careers & Employability Support
- Deliver practical employability activities and careers exploration sessions.
- Coordinate employer talks, careers events and workplace visits.
- Facilitate mock interviews and recruitment exercises.
- Support participants to understand different career pathways and labour market opportunities.
- Promote progression into employment, apprenticeships, education and training.

Partnership & Community Engagement
- Coordinate delivery with:
- Community Organisations
- Employers
- Education Providers
- Youth Services
- Local Authorities
- Specialist Support Providers
- Manage activity schedules, venues and logistics.
- Promote activities through face-to-face and digital engagement methods.
- Support outreach events and participant recruitment activity.
- Build strong relationships that enhance opportunities for participants.

Safeguarding, Inclusion & Wellbeing
- Promote a safe, inclusive and respectful learning environment.
- Support participants with diverse needs and backgrounds.
- Recognise and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns.
- Promote equality, diversity and inclusion in all aspects of delivery.
- Manage group dynamics positively and professionally.
- Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

Quality, Compliance & Performance
- Complete activity plans, risk assessments and evaluation reports.
- Maintain accurate records of attendance, participation and outcomes.
- Monitor engagement and progression against programme objectives.
- Collect participant feedback and use insights to improve delivery.
- Ensure compliance with safeguarding, GDPR, health & safety and quality standards.
- Support programme targets and positive participant outcomes.

Essential Criteria
- Experience planning, coordinating and delivering engaging activities for young people or young adults.
- Strong facilitation, presentation and group engagement skills.
- Ability to motivate and inspire individuals from diverse backgrounds.
- Experience supporting personal development, employability or progression outcomes.
- Understanding of barriers affecting young people, including:
- Low confidence
- Poor mental wellbeing
- Disability
- Neurodiversity
- Housing challenges
- Digital exclusion
- Limited work experience
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational and event coordination skills.
- Good IT skills including Microsoft Office and digital engagement tools.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and activities simultaneously.

Transferable Skills Welcome
We welcome applications from candidates with backgrounds in:
- Youth Work
- Employability Services
- Careers Guidance
- Education & Training
- Sports Development
- Community Development
- Coaching & Mentoring
- Creative Arts
- Outdoor Education
- Social Care
- Housing Support
- Volunteering Programmes
- Customer Engagement
- Apprenticeships
- Mental Health & Wellbeing Services

If you have experience motivating people, running activities, building relationships and helping others achieve positive outcomes, we would love to hear from you.

Desirable Criteria
- Qualification in Youth Work, Teaching, Coaching, Careers Guidance, Employability or a related field.
- First Aid qualification.
- Experience delivering employability or personal development programmes.
- Experience coordinating events, projects or community initiatives.
- Knowledge of local labour markets, training pathways and apprenticeships.
- Understanding of safeguarding and working with vulnerable young people.

Additional Information
- Community-based role with regular travel across the local area.
- No homeworking due to the nature of the role.
- Enhanced DBS checks may be required.
- Flexibility to work across multiple venues and occasional non-standard hours where required.
- Ongoing training and professional development provided.

title: Administrator
description: The De Parys Group has an exciting opportunity for an administrator to join our busy practice support team and assist in the smooth delivery of excellent patient care. This role is offered on a full time basis, working 37.5 hours per week. You will be required to provide an efficient, accurate and confidential clinical administration & secretarial service, supporting clinicians, patients and the wider practice team. The postholder will contribute to effective administrative & referral management, patient care coordination, clinical correspondence and the delivery of practice and PCN requirements. Provide comprehensive administrative support to clinicians and the wider practice team. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails, scanning and other general administrative duties. Maintain accurate electronic and paper records. Manage telephone and patient enquiries professionally and appropriately. Undertake audio typing, clinical correspondence, reports and referrals. Process and monitor referrals through e-RS, including rejected referrals and advice & guidance. Coordinate urgent, cancer, specialist, diagnostic, pathology and secondary care pathways. Monitor outstanding actions and escalate delays or concerns appropriately. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice protocols. Support the practice's adult and child safeguarding administration, including confidential documentation and reports. Process private work, including insurance, DVLA and patient letter requests, including invoicing where required. Work collaboratively within the administrative and clinical teams and provide appropriate cover during colleague absence. Undertake chaperone duties following appropriate training, where required. Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role as requested by the line manager or team leader. If you would like to find out more information about this role, please see the attached job specification.
